Gerai. Iron hoe. Long narrow blade, dipped in the middle and chipped. Straight back edge with a central cylindrical socket.
Abu Sekakin. Part of a lion trap. Iron blade made from two pieces of metal held together with a central rivet. The blade is oblong and attached to a long length of twisted rope.

Circular bird trap of wooden hoop with network of string to which is attached a number of horse hair nooses. Tied to one side of the hoop is a long length of twisted string with a wooden peg at the end.
Firneip. Trap, originally described as a springe trap or stick and noose. Length of wood, tapered at one end; thin cord tied between the ends, like a bow, and with a small cylinder of wood tied on.

arms.title: Couteau à moissonner
Hache
Axe for making ostrich eggshell beads, with narrow iron blade and wooden handle. [El.B 'DCF 2004-2006 What's Upstairs?' 10/11/2005]
Reaping knife, with a metal blade and wooden handle. [AB [OPS Move] 19/12/2016]

Spear with a wooden shaft and pointed spearhead. Split socket is integral to the spearhead. Shaft has a circular cross-section and tapers slightly towards the terminal; band of metal wrapped around the shaft near the terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is large and leaf shaped, with a midrib, ridges that follow the outside edge; split socket. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of metal wire are two points on the shaft, and one coil of metal at the terminal.

Risha or Um Rish. Spear of royal type with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is long and leaf shaped with a midrib and ridges following the outside edges. Split socket has a circular cross-section, and flares slightly below the shoulders. The shaft has a circular cross-section and is slightly tapered. Made for Shartai [a district administrative chief].

Hunting spear for lions, with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is long and leaf shaped with a midrib and a ridge following the outside edges. The shanks has two large triple pointed prongs; two points have come away from one of the prongs. At the bottom of the shank is a square section with a hole at the centre; split socket. The shaft has a circular cross-section.

Throwing knife made of iron with a printed cotton cloth grip. the main blade is slightly curved, with a recurved terminal and midrib, The side blade is straight with a pointed terminal. The cloth grip is red with green, yellow and black design.
A straight wooden club or digging stick. End enlarged and pointed, with band of line engraving.
Knife with iron blade and wooden handle. Double-edged blade with tang set into a wooden handle which flares towards the butt.
Flattened wooden throwing stick with a long, straight handle and an axe-like head; head is pointed at one end, and blunt at the other. Bark is still present on wood on one edge.
Flattened wooden throwing stick with long, straight handle and axe-like head. One end of head is narrower than the other. Cracks present in wood.

Spear of Shelakai type, with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The spearhead is large and leaf shaped, with a midrib and faint ridges following the outside edge; short split socket with a circular cross-section is attached to the shaft with a hide collar. The shaft has a circular cross-section with, and a coil of metal around the terminal.

Spear of Shelakai type, with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The spearhead is large and leaf shaped, with a midrib and faint ridges following the outside edge; short split socket with a circular cross-section. The shaft has a circular cross-section tapering slightly towards the terminal.

Knife with iron blade, wooden handle and leather sheath. Double-edged blade with tang set into a waisted wooden handle with oval cross-section at blade and circular at butt; tang extends from butt of handle and is bent over to hold it in place; leather sheath with loop handle wrapped with leather thong; decorated with three ridges near the mouth and indented geometric designs; length of plant fibre and possible sinew around sheath. Handle is broken in a number of places but worn smooth through subsequent use; blade cannot be removed from sheath.

Knife with iron blade, wooden handle and leather sheath. Short double-edged blade with grip with waisted wooden handle flaring towards blade and butt; length of metal wire wrapped around handle; red and black leather sheath with loop handle. Blade cannot be removed from sheath.

Knife with iron blade, wooden handle and leather sheath. Double-edged blade with slight midrib; tang set into a waisted wooden handle with oval cross-section at blade and circular at butt; blade incised with a five-pointed star on both sides; red and black leather sheath with loop handle, decorated with three ridges near the mouth and indented geometric designs.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal blade. The blade is leaf shaped with a midrib; socket is possibly split but the edges are joined. The shaft has a circular cross-section with a flat terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and pointed spearhead. Shaft has a lozenge shaped projection decorated with geometric grooves, with square projections at both ends; short split socket. The shaft has a circular cross-section and has a plaited hide band, and a wrapped strip of metal at the terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and metal point. The spearhead tapers to a point and has a circular cross-section, with a protruding rectangular shank decorated with geometric grooves. The split socket is short with edges meeting. Shaft has a circular cross-section with a flat terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is small, with angular shoulders and cutting edge. The shank has a flat cross-section, decorated with grooves and cross-hatching, with downward facing barbs on both edges. The socket is decorated with a geometric section near the shank. The shaft has a circular cross-section with a metal coil around the terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is small and leaf shaped. The shank has a rectangular cross-section, with downward facing barbs on both sides. The top of the socket has a square cross-section, followed by a rectangular section with small barbs; the bottom of the split socket has a circular cross-section. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of metal at the terminal.

Spear with a wooden shaft and iron spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped with a midrib. The shank has a rectangular cross-section, decorated with vertical grooves, with thick barbs along both edges; split socket. The shaft has a circular cross-section with a coil of metal around the terminal.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The leaf-shaped blade has slight midrib and bevelled edges; the shank has a square cross-section; two of the faces feature a feathered left and right edge, formed of evenly spaced downward-angled grooves. The socket is closed, flaring slightly towards the mouth. The wooden shaft is plain with a circular cross-section. The butt has a weight at its end in the form of a coiled strip of flattened metal.

An axe with a wooden handle and metal blade, engraved at the narrow part with cross hatching in between rows of punchmarks, and patterns of triangles, dots and rings; butt of blade engraved with two circles.

An axe with a wooden handle and metal blade. The blade is engraved with grooves along the two long edges; in the centre are two flaring rectangles, filled with diamonds, with three lines extending from them, one topped with a triangle and two topped with a 'u' shape. Decoration is repeated on the reverse.

Throwing spear used on horseback, with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped with angular shoulders, a midrib and grooves along the outside edges. The shanks is short with a rectangular cross-section; decorated with zigzags with short barbs on both edges. The split socket is long with a circular cross-section. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of metal part way down, and a coil of metal at the terminal.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is small and leaf shaped with a faint midrib; two down-turned barbs below the shoulders of the blade. The shank has a square cross-section decorated with chevrons; two additional barbs facing different ways on the shank. The socket has a square section near the shank with short barbs on the edges. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of fibre part-way down from the socket.

Surat el Meiram. Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped, with midrib and ridges following the outside edge. The shank is made up of geometric sections, decorated with grooves; long socket with a circular cross-section. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of metal around the terminal. Made by Nureim Shukeir for Ali Dinar.

Surat el Meiram. Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is long and leaf shaped, with midrib and ridges following the outside edge. The shank has an octagonal section and is decorated with grooves and zigzags; the socket has a circular cross section. The shaft has a circular cross-section. Made by Toto for Sultan Ali Dinar.

Surat el Meiram. Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped, with midrib and faint ridges following the outside edge. The socket is split into three sections and has a circular cross section; decorated with cross hatching, zigzags and grooves. The shaft has a circular cross-section.

Sendi Itti. Spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is short and leaf shaped with a faint midrib, decorated with faint grooves and three rings below the shoulder. The socket is decorated with three rings midway down. The shaft has a circular cross-section, with a coil of metal at the terminal.

Risha or Um Rish. Spear with a metal spearhead and a wooden shaft. The spearhead has a leaf shaped blade with a shallow midrib and bevelled edges. The slender shank has a circular cross-section, flaring to a closed socket. The shaft is plain with a circular cross-section.

Risha or Um Rish. Spear with a metal spearhead and a wooden shaft. The spearhead has a leaf shaped blade with a shallow midrib and bevelled edges. The slender shank has a circular cross-section, flaring to a closed socket. The shaft is plain with a circular cross-section. The butt has a weight at its end formed from a coiled strip of flattened metal.

garment.title: Shakir. A reproduction of a padded, quilted horseman's coat, with rectangular sleeves and a body that flares out slightly at the bottom. It has a raised collar and a slit down from the front of the neckline, and a slit up from the middle of the bottom hem up to the waist. It is made of vertical striped silk of pink, yellow, green and black, lined on the inside with black and white gingham cotton fabric. The neckline, bottom hem, central slit and wrist cuffs are decorated with blue trim. Some areas of the coat have significantly faded due to light.

masks-ritual.title: Incense burner. Made by joining 3 small pedestalled bowls. At the intersection is a triple arched handle over the bowls. The flaring pedestals are coil made; the bowls beaten of clay tempered with organic matter, slipped with red haematite & mica. Red interior. The handle, bowl rims & body pedestal junctions are painted white and black. [Alicia Bell [OPS move] 29/06/2016]

Incense burner of red ware, slipped with Haematite. Bowl set on a pedestal foot. The foot has an expanded rim and then narrows to the bottom of the bowl. The rim of the bowl and the foot are decorated with white pigment on which black lines are painted. There are also black and white bands below the rim and on the pedestal. There are also two Arabic inscriptions on the sides of the bowl. [MOBB [OPS move] 30/06/2016]
